name: Romanian (ACLro) — Institutul Limbii Române, CEFR A1 through C2
material_vintage: Itemised 2026-09-19 (course rebuilt 2026-09-22). The 30 can-do items (RO-<level>-CD-*) reproduce, in paraphrase, the wording of the Council of Europe's CEFR Table 2 Self-assessment Grid (Listening, Reading, Spoken Interaction, Spoken Production, Writing for A1-C2), fetched from the official Europass PDF mirror of the Council of Europe document and cross-checked against the CEFR Table 1 Global Scale page on coe.int. The grammar (G) and vocabulary/topic (V) items per level itemise the standard teaching sequence used for Romanian as a foreign language (as taught by Institutul Limbii Române / ACLro-style courses and comparable RFL textbooks: a fi/a avea and the four verb conjugations at A1; perfect compus, reflexives and near future at A2; imperfect, subjunctive and reported speech at B1; full subjunctive/conditional, passive and the vocative at B2; register and idiom at C1-C2) and were completed from general, well-established knowledge of Romanian grammar and pedagogy rather than from a single numbered official curriculum document, since ACLro/ILR publish sample tests and level descriptions but not a single itemised numbered syllabus equivalent to a UK exam-board spec. This is flagged for re-verification against ILR's published sample-test pages if a more granular official item list becomes available. Facts about Romanian grammar (three genders including neuter, the noun-suffixed definite article, the vocative case, periphrastic future/subjunctive constructions, clitic pronoun forms) are accurate standard Romanian-linguistics content.
level_source: learner-declared, no external framework available (as a single RQF level): placed at level 2. The course itself spans CEFR A1-C2, and each stage records its own CEFR level.
framework: Council of Europe Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR), six levels A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2, each defined by a Global Scale descriptor and, per skill, by the Table 2 Self-assessment Grid descriptors for Listening, Reading, Spoken Interaction, Spoken Production and Writing. Romanian-specific instruction follows the Institutul Limbii Române (ILR) / ACLro framework for Romanian as a foreign/heritage language, which certifies learners against these same CEFR levels through its own placement and level tests.
